Legs.Subject: MaximumModulus is exactly 2^62, and Create REFUSES it and every value above it with an ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the 'modulus' parameter — at the ceiling itself, one above it, and both carrier extremes. The bound is a REPRESENTATION invariant rather than a policy: it is what keeps Add and Subtract a single conditional fold, because two representatives then sum below 2^63 and never overflow the carrier
every rung of the committed fifteen-rung modulus ladder, BEFORE Create is ever handed it
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality — trial division by the primes below 8192 and then twenty BigInteger strong-probable-prime rounds. No ladder constant is taken on its word, which is the same distrust binary-field.product-and-reduction-vs-oracle shows its own five moduli; a mistyped rung fails HERE, by name, rather than silently weakening every other case that runs the ladder. Both sides EXACT, so the substrate condition does not arise. ENVELOPE, and it is not the same statement at both ends of the ladder: the six rungs at or below 8191² = 67092481 are decided by TRIAL DIVISION, which shares no idea with anything in Puck.Maths, while the nine above it are decided by the twenty BigInteger rounds — whose base set opens with two, the base PrimeField64's own machineword IsPrime and its Baillie composition both run. Those nine rungs therefore share the CRITERION with the type they gate and differ in arithmetic, in base set and in loop structure only

Legs.Subject: Create ACCEPTS every ladder rung the oracle proved prime, and the field it returns reports that modulus back, answers One as 1 and Zero as 0, equals a second field built over the same modulus — the record's whole value being its modulus — and PRINTS as exactly that one datum: ToString emits the modulus alone, the guarded identities kept out of the rendering by a hand-written PrintMembers because they are constants of the type rather than carried state

an EVEN modulus is REFUSED with an ArgumentException naming 'modulus' at zero, two, four, six, 65536 and the largest even value below the ceiling. TWO is the historical corner and the reason the ladder carries it: the guard read `2 == (modulus & 1)`, a comparison a one-bit mask can never satisfy, so Create(2) was reachable and TrySqrt's non-residue walk never returned there
Create's composite refusal over an odd-composite ladder — 1, 9, 15, 25, 561, and FOUR OF the psi_k strong pseudoprimes: the ones that force bases four, six, eight and eleven
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality, which independently classifies every one of them composite BEFORE the refusal is demanded. The psi rows are the discriminating ones: a modulus admitted on a short witness set would be a COMPOSITE modulus in a type whose whole contract is that the quotient ring is a field. ENVELOPE, twofold. EIGHT distinct psi values fit below the 2^62 ceiling rather than four; the other four force bases one, two, three and five and are exercised against IsPrime by prime-field.is-prime-vs-sieve-and-witness-ladder, not against Create's gate here. And the oracle is shared-nothing only over the low rows: 1, 9, 15, 25 and 561 are settled by TRIAL DIVISION, while all four psi rows sit above 8191² = 67092481 and are settled by twenty BigInteger rounds whose base set opens with the base-two round PrimeField64's Baillie–PSW decision also runs — so those rows share that criterion and differ in arithmetic and in the Lucas half

Legs.Subject: a DEFAULT-INITIALIZED PrimeField64 is reachable — the record struct's private constructor does not stop `default(PrimeField64)`, and neither does an unassigned array element, which this case reaches through as well — and it REFUSES its whole semantic surface with InvalidOperationException: One, Zero, Add, Subtract, Negate, Multiply, Inverse, LegendreCharacter, Pow, both Reduce overloads, TrySqrt, and BatchInverse at length zero and length three. Each row is named in the failure text, so a member that quietly answers is reported as itself. The EMPTY batch is the row with teeth: the descriptor is read before the span is, so the zero-length early return cannot let an uninitialized field through unremarked. Modulus is deliberately OUTSIDE the policy and still reads zero, which is what keeps a default value printable and comparable — the array row asserts that equality still holds against `default`, and PRINTABILITY is asserted on ToString itself: a hand-written PrintMembers prints the modulus alone, so a default value formats as `PrimeField64 { Modulus = 0 }` instead of throwing from the guarded identities the compiler-synthesized member walk would have read. This statement REPLACES the earlier pin, under which Add, Subtract and Negate returned unreduced integer arithmetic with no diagnostic while Multiply, Reduce and Pow happened to raise DivideByZeroException from the zero modulus; that split was the defect rather than the contract, and the type now follows the house pattern FixedRateAccumulator sets
PrimeField64.Add, Subtract, Negate and Multiply at every rung of the six-modulus ladder, on both swept operands folded into [0, p)
Legs.Against: one exact BigInteger residue expression per operation, inline in Subjects.PrimeFieldArithmeticExact — (a + b) % p, ((a − b) % p + p) % p, ((−a) % p + p) % p and (a·b) % p. BOTH SIDES ARE EXACT, so condition (B) — the shared rounding substrate — drops out entirely: there is no rounding here to be shared, and agreement is bit-for-bit or nothing. The derivation routes differ where the kernels branch: the subject folds Add with ONE conditional subtraction that leans on p < 2^62, writes Subtract as a borrow-avoiding two-arm compare, and widens Multiply to UInt128 for a single hardware remainder, where the oracle forms each value in arbitrary width and takes one remainder with no case analysis at all

Legs.Subject: both Reduce overloads, pinned BEFORE anything leans on them — the unsigned fold on the reinterpreted sixty-four-bit draw, and the signed fold on the raw itself
Legs.Against: value % p and ((value % p) + p) % p in BigInteger, inline in the same claim. The signed overload's whole content is that a negative value folds UP by the modulus, and long.MinValue is in the swept edge set, where the C# remainder's sign rule is the one thing that could go wrong

Legs.Subject: every answer is REDUCED: Add, Subtract, Negate and Multiply all land strictly below the modulus at every ladder rung, which is the representation invariant the whole type rests on and the invariant a wrong fold breaks first

the identities and the two inverses close: Zero is a two-sided additive identity, One a two-sided multiplicative one, Negate(a) is a's additive inverse, and subtracting b undoes adding it — statements that need no reference at all and that a modulus-fold defect cannot satisfy accidentally

ENVELOPE: at the p = 3 rung the fold has three images, so that rung pins the guards and the degenerate branches rather than the wide arithmetic. The wide arithmetic is pinned at the 2^62 − 57 rung, where the fold is essentially uniform over the whole field and Multiply's UInt128 intermediate is at its widest; the ladder is declared so that both ends are swept on every operand

PrimeField64.Pow at five ladder rungs and five exponents per operand — the swept full-width exponent, zero, one, p − 2 and (p − 1)/2 — which is this family's HOT PATH: Inverse, LegendreCharacter, TrySqrt's descent and all four primality entry points reach their arithmetic through this one chain
Legs.Against: BigInteger.ModPow, inline in Subjects.PrimeFieldPowMatchesModularPower. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. The routes differ in REPRESENTATION, not merely in code: the subject converts into ScaledResidueRing64 once, runs square-and-multiply with a per-bit conditional multiply, and converts back once, so every intermediate is a Montgomery image; the oracle stays in plain residues from first to last. A representation leak — the second of this family's named failure modes — is exactly what disagreement here catches

Legs.Subject: the exponent's two poles are exact rather than approximated: the zeroth power is One for EVERY base including zero, which is the documented convention, and the first power moves nothing

Fermat's little theorem closes the chain at every rung: a^(p−1) is One for every non-zero a and zero for a = 0, a statement whose truth depends on the modulus really being prime and so on Create's own gate, which prime-field.create-and-refusals pins against the oracle

ENVELOPE: Pow's operation count depends on the exponent and the routine is deliberately NOT constant-time in it, so nothing here is a timing statement. What the five-exponent ladder buys is schedule breadth — a zero-bit exponent, a one-bit exponent, and two exponents whose expansions are dense across the whole width — not a claim about the shape of the chain

PrimeField64.Inverse and BatchInverse over a length ladder of 0, 1, 2, 3, 511, 512, 513 and 1024 elements — the ladder that straddles BatchInverse's 512-element stackalloc/ArrayPool boundary in BOTH directions
Legs.Against: BigInteger.ModPow at exponent p − 2, computed per element and inline in Subjects.PrimeFieldInverseAndBatch. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. The routes differ where it matters: the subject's batch accumulates a running product, inverts ONCE, and peels each element back off that single inverse in a backward pass, so an element's answer depends on every OTHER element in the region — a coupling the per-element oracle has no way to reproduce and a transposed prefix index would break immediately. ENVELOPE, because the two arms are NOT the same statement: for the SCALAR Inverse the reference shares the derivation. PrimeField64.Inverse is Pow(value, Modulus − 2) (PrimeField64.cs:382-386) and the reference is BigInteger.ModPow at that same exponent — Fermat against Fermat, differing in REPRESENTATION (Montgomery form against plain residues) and not in theorem, on an exponent prime-field.pow-vs-modpow already sweeps. What the scalar arm adds over that case is the delegation and the zero guard; the independent content of THIS case is the batch's running-product coupling

Legs.Subject: the scalar and the batch agree element for element at every ladder length, and every returned value multiplies with its input to One — so the batch is pinned twice over, against the oracle and against its own scalar sibling

zero has no inverse anywhere: Inverse REFUSES it with a DivideByZeroException, and BatchInverse refuses a region containing one at the first, a middle and the last index, because the shared running product is then zero

a REFUSED batch leaves the region bit-for-bit untouched. That is not decoration: the forward pass writes only its own scratch and the throw lands before the backward pass writes anything, so the failure is atomic — and the pooled scratch is returned in a finally on that path too
an EMPTY region is a no-op rather than a refusal, which is the early return the method opens with and the one length at which no scratch is taken at all

ENVELOPE: the 1024-element rung runs at the 2^62 − 57 modulus only, and the short ladder at the remaining rungs. What that buys is the POOLED path exercised once at the widest arithmetic the type admits rather than four times over; the stack path is exercised at every rung. deep.prime-field-inverse-and-batch runs the long ladder at every rung instead. The rented array is longer than the request, and nothing here reads past the requested count

the POOLED scratch is CLEARED before it re-enters the shared pool: after a 1024-element batch, an immediate same-thread rent of the same bucket — the request ArrayPool.Shared serves from its thread-local slot, so an uncleared return would hand the very same array straight back — no longer carries the batch's first three hand-derived running products a0, a0·a1, a0·a1·a2. The kernel is the shared BatchInverseKernel, so the one clear covers QuadraticExtensionField64.BatchInverse and every future ring the kernel serves
PrimeField64.LegendreCharacter at five ladder rungs on the folded swept operand — Euler's exponentiation criterion, one Montgomery chain per call
Legs.Against: Oracles.JacobiSymbolReciprocity — the binary quadratic-reciprocity descent in BigInteger, which at a PRIME modulus is the Legendre symbol. A genuinely different derivation route rather than a re-spelling: the subject raises to (p − 1)/2 and reads the answer off a power, the oracle never exponentiates at all. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. The oracle calls NO Puck.Maths member — in particular it is not NumberTheoryFunctions.JacobiSymbol, which is a SUBJECT of core.jacobi-symbol-cross-carrier, nor UnsignedNumberFunctions.JacobiSymbol, which IsStrongLucasProbablePrime itself calls

Legs.Subject: the same character, a second time
Legs.Against: BigInteger.ModPow at exponent (p − 1)/2, inline in the same claim body — the THIRD route, and the one that anchors the reciprocity descent itself rather than merely the subject. Two references that share nothing with each other and nothing with the subject must both agree, so a defect in the new oracle cannot pass as agreement

Legs.Subject: the character is MULTIPLICATIVE on the swept pair — the character of a product is the product of the characters, zeros included — and a square always reports +1. Neither statement can be satisfied by a reciprocity descent that lost its sign or by an exponentiation that lost its bit
the character is exactly zero at zero and never at any other reduced element, which is the one branch LegendreCharacter takes before it exponentiates at all

ENVELOPE: the law folds every operand into [0, p) before it asks. LegendreCharacter does NOT enforce its reduced-operand precondition, and an unreduced argument reaches Encode, which folds it — so an unreduced multiple of p would be reported as a non-square rather than as zero. That regime is outside this statement by construction. It cannot leak through the extension factory: extension-field.construction-and-refusals proves Create rejects the modulus and other unreduced generators BEFORE consulting the character, which is the validating boundary responsible for enforcing LegendreCharacter's hot-path precondition
TrySqrt's ACCEPT/REJECT decision at five ladder rungs — a decision it makes for itself, before any root exists, by raising the operand to (p − 1)/2 inside the ring
Legs.Against: Oracles.JacobiSymbolReciprocity: the operand is a square exactly when the reciprocity symbol is not −1. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out, and the routes could not be further apart — one exponentiates in Montgomery form, the other descends by reciprocity in BigInteger and never forms a power

Legs.Subject: the root is checked by SQUARING IT BACK rather than against a reference root, which is the only honest statement available: a square has two roots and the method promises neither one in particular. Both roots are exercised — the returned r and its sibling Negate(r) = p − r — and both must square back to the operand; the two coincide only at zero
a REFUSED TrySqrt returns false AND leaves zero in the out parameter, at every rung, so the failed call carries no stale value out
zero roots to zero and returns true, the one operand that short-circuits ahead of the character decision entirely

the character TrySqrt decides for itself agrees with LegendreCharacter on the SAME operand stream — the two cases share the domain key prime-field-root, so this is a statement about identical operands rather than about two sweeps that happen to overlap

the ladder straddles BOTH of TrySqrt's arms, and the claim ASSERTS that rather than assuming it: rungs congruent to 3 modulo 4 take the direct power value^((p + 1)/4), rungs congruent to 1 modulo 4 take the nonresidue-assisted descent, and the body counts both and fails if the ladder ever stops carrying one. The 3·2^30 + 1 rung is the deep descent — a 2-adic valuation of 30 in p − 1, so the correction loop runs many rounds — and the 17 rung is its degenerate opposite, where the odd part of p − 1 is ONE

ENVELOPE: the descent's walk to the smallest non-residue is an UNBOUNDED search with no step budget and a ulong counter that could in principle wrap. Its termination rests on a theorem (non-residues are half the non-zero residues), not on a validation, so a defect that made the ring's minus-one unreachable would HANG rather than redden this law. A hang is not a red test. An unbounded search whose predicate is a subject owes two clauses with DISTINCT messages — a deterministic step budget, which names a broken predicate, and a wrap guard, which names an exhausted range. The subject has neither, and no law can supply one from outside — so the failure mode is named here because nothing in this suite can catch it
PrimeExtensions.IsPrime at EVERY value through 20,000 — even, odd, zero and one included
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeSieve, an ordinary sieve of Eratosthenes. This is the family's strongest anchor and the reason it comes first: the sieve carries no notion of a witness, a base, an exponent or a Montgomery form, so it shares with the subject not merely no code but no IDEA. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. It is exhaustive over its band rather than sampled, so nothing in that band is a matter of luck

Legs.Subject: rejection of the published leading-prime-base pseudoprimes
Legs.Against: Subjects.PrimeFieldWitnessPseudoprimes — eight (value, leading-base-count) rows drawn from the published psi_k table
Legs.Citation: psi_k is the LEAST composite that is a strong probable prime to the first k prime bases. The chain matters, because it is the LEAST-ness that this leg's counting rests on and it is not all one author's: Jaeschke (1993) determined psi_1 through psi_8 exactly and gave psi_9, psi_10 and psi_11 ≤ 3825123056546413051 as a BOUND, which later work proved least; Sorenson and Webster (2015) settled psi_12 = 318665857834031151167461 and psi_13. Each row's base count is DERIVED from that table rather than captured from any implementation: a value strictly below psi_(k+1) survives at most k leading bases, and psi_7 == psi_8 and psi_9 == psi_10 == psi_11 are why two rows read 8 and 11 rather than the indices the values are tabulated under. Every count is then MEASURED in the law by Oracles.ModularStrongProbablePrime, so a mistranscribed row fails rather than passing quietly

Legs.Subject: Each tabulated composite is checked against the independent reference's leading-prime-base survival count before rejection by the exact machineword decision is demanded. The rows have counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 11. ENVELOPE: these counts describe the reference's first-prime-base criterion; production's wide-word decision uses Baillie-PSW, so this law pins its rejection of these composites rather than its witness set.

IsPrime over a twenty-five-value carrier ladder — both sides of 2^31, 2^32, 2^61, 2^62 and 2^63, the largest prime below 2^32, the three values at the top of the carrier, and the smallest values where the guards outnumber the arithmetic
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality. ENVELOPE, stated rather than implied: through 8191² = 67092481 — just under 2^26 — that oracle decides by TRIAL DIVISION alone and shares no idea with the subject; above that band it runs twenty BigInteger strong-probable-prime rounds and so shares the base-two CRITERION, differing in arithmetic (plain residues versus one shared ScaledResidueRing64) and in what follows that round: above uint the subject is Baillie–PSW, a base-two strong round and a strong Lucas test with Selfridge Method A, where the oracle runs nineteen more prime-base rounds. That upper leg therefore pins the subject's arithmetic, its Montgomery encoding and its base-two round, and checks its Lucas half only through agreement — and does not independently re-derive the completeness theorem, which is a third-party computation on both sides

Legs.Subject: PrimeExtensions.IsPrime over the swept candidate stream — both drawn raws read as ulong and each additionally forced odd, so the sweep meets the arithmetic and not only the even short-circuit — across the WHOLE carrier, which is where the sieve band cannot reach
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. ENVELOPE, the same one prime-field.is-prime-vs-sieve-and-witness-ladder's ladder leg states and stated again because this law lives almost entirely above it: through 8191² the oracle is trial division and shares no idea with the subject; above it the oracle runs twenty BigInteger rounds against the subject's Baillie–PSW above uint (one Montgomery base-two strong round and a strong Lucas test), so the base-two criterion is shared and the arithmetic and the Lucas half are not

Legs.Subject: the edge battery is what makes this sweep bite rather than merely run: read as ulong, the committed edge set carries 0, 1, 2^64 − 1, 2^63, 2^63 ± 1, 2^31 ± 1, 2^47 ± 1 and the two's-complement images of every negative raw, so the carrier's corners — where the odd-part split, the trailing-zero count and the ring's radix reduction are all at their extremes — are swept on every run rather than sampled

MIRROR-ADJACENT, and named so no reader over-reads it: this law SAMPLES where prime-field.montgomery-chains-exhaustive sweeps EVERY value from zero through 10^6 against a sieve of Eratosthenes and the whole contiguous 100,000-value band at 9·10^11 against a segmented one. That law is the gate of record for SCALE, at the Exhaustive tier; this law is the gate of record for the statement, at Default

PrimeField64.IsStrongProbablePrime over the swept candidate stream at six witness bases per candidate — the swept full-width base, zero, one, two, value − 1 and value itself — on both the drawn value and its forced-odd image
Legs.Against: Oracles.ModularStrongProbablePrime, one strong round evaluated entirely in BigInteger. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. The routes differ in REPRESENTATION rather than in criterion, and that is the point: the subject never leaves Montgomery form, comparing its power against the ring's own encoded One and NegativeOne, where the oracle compares plain residues against 1 and value − 1. A representation leak is what disagreement catches; the criterion itself is shared and this leg does not claim otherwise

Legs.Subject: the contract's own zero-base clause, which is the one clause a reader would not guess: a base that reduces to zero carries no evidence and PASSES. Both witness = 0 and witness = value are exercised at every ODD candidate above two, and the oracle carries the same clause, so the two AGREE about it rather than one of them merely implementing it. ENVELOPE, and it is where this clause actually lives: the clause sits BELOW the guards in subject and oracle alike, so an even candidate is rejected before its base is ever reduced and the zero base does not pass there — which the guard row below states directly rather than leaving as an apparent exception

the direction a probable-prime test decides OUTRIGHT: every prime passes every base. The candidate's primality is settled independently by Oracles.ExactPrimality and, where it is prime, all six rounds are required to accept — so a false REJECT is caught here, which is the failure a differential against a probable-prime sibling can never see
the guards below the arithmetic: values under two are rejected, two is accepted, and every even value above two is rejected, at every base

ENVELOPE: a passed round proves nothing about primality and this law never says it does. What it pins is that the round is the round it CLAIMS to be. The composition's own thesis — that this round's pseudoprimes and the Lucas test's are disjoint populations — is pinned in prime-field.pseudoprime-populations, not here. This law and its two neighbours share the domain key prime-field-primality, so all three speak about one candidate stream
PrimeField64.IsStrongLucasProbablePrime over the swept candidate stream, forced odd, across the WHOLE carrier
Legs.Against: Oracles.StrongLucasSelfridge — the same test computed from 2×2 COMPANION-MATRIX powers in BigInteger. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out. Three deliberate divergences make this independent rather than a re-spelling: the subject walks the norm-one trace ladder most-significant-bit first, carrying the traces C_k = z^k + z^-k of z = a / b in Montgomery form with no power of Q, and reads U_d = 0 and V_d = 0 off the trace pair (C_h, C_(h+1)) at half the index, while the oracle multiplies matrices in plain residues, carries no V recurrence and no trace at all — it derives V_d from two consecutive U terms — and reads U_d directly. A wrong cross term, a wrong reciprocal of Q, a sign of Q read off the wrong magnitude class, or an acceptance test that is not equivalent to U_d = 0 or V_d = 0 shows here; prime-field.lucas-trace-ladder-vs-recurrence adds every odd value of a contiguous band and every small Q directly. It is also O(log n), so this leg reaches the whole carrier where an index-by-index recurrence oracle would stop in the tens of thousands

Legs.Subject: the Selfridge Method A parameter search — the discriminant the whole test is defined by
Legs.Against: the same search inside Oracles.StrongLucasSelfridge, walking SIGNED BigInteger candidates with the sign carried explicitly (the subject reads it off `magnitude & 3`) and taking its symbol from Oracles.JacobiSymbolReciprocity, this suite's own reciprocity descent. This CLOSES the OWED that stands over any Lucas oracle taking its symbol from NumberTheoryFunctions.JacobiSymbol, the BigInteger sibling of the very function the subject's search reads its symbols from: a wrong symbol would pick the same discriminant on both sides. Here it cannot: the two symbols are separate implementations with no shared line. This leg is also what licenses the UnsignedNumberFunctions.JacobiSymbol citation on this case: the subject's search reads that member's SIGN at every swept candidate — through residue masks derived from it once for magnitudes below 64, through the member itself beyond — and inverting the returned sign reddens this law together with prime-field.baillie-composition and prime-field.pseudoprime-populations. What the citation claims is the sign and nothing wider — the cross-carrier agreement and the composite-modulus regime are core.jacobi-symbol-cross-carrier, where the composite regime stands against the symbol's factor-and-Euler DEFINITION rather than against the library's own sibling descent, and the class this law cannot reach is the ENVELOPE below

Legs.Subject: the direction the test decides outright: EVERY PRIME PASSES. The candidate's primality is settled independently by Oracles.ExactPrimality, and where it is prime the test is required to accept — a false reject that no differential against another probable-prime test could see

perfect squares are rejected, at the adversarial shape: the square of a large value, where no small factor screens it out and the parameter search would otherwise run to the value's least prime factor. The oracle decides squareness by BISECTION on the root — exact, float-free, thirty-two halvings — deliberately NOT by the subject's own ulong.SquareRoot, whose first estimate comes from hardware floating point and is the single floating-point touch the whole wing admits to. A gate must not read the estimate it gates

ENVELOPE: the Selfridge search is UNBOUNDED — no step budget, and its ulong magnitude counter can wrap. Its termination rests on a theorem rather than on a validation, so a defect that suppressed the −1 outcome would hang or wrap rather than redden this law; wrapped, the sign is read off `magnitude & 3`, which is meaningless for an even magnitude. An unbounded search whose predicate is a subject owes two clauses with DISTINCT messages — a deterministic step budget, which names a broken predicate, and a wrap guard, which names an exhausted range — and the wrap half is not hypothetical: FirstPrimeAtOrAbove(2^64 − 40) returned 3, having stepped past the carrier and wrapped, a wrong ANSWER that no step budget can catch. The subject has neither clause, and no law can supply one from outside. Stated here because nothing in this suite can catch it. It is also the exact boundary of this case's UnsignedNumberFunctions.JacobiSymbol citation, and the campaign probed both sides of it: inverting the symbol's returned sign REDDENS this law, while perturbing the two-indicator shift so the −1 outcome is never produced HANGS the run instead

ENVELOPE: the perfect-square check, which runs once the tabulated candidates below magnitude 64 are exhausted, is a COST bound and not a termination guarantee — candidates step by two and so sweep every odd number, one of which shares a factor with the value, and the vanishing-symbol exit fires there anyway — so this law's square rows pin the ANSWER at squares and say nothing about why the search halts. Delete the guard and n = 25 still returns after one candidate and n = 9 after six; what it buys is COST, since without it a square spends Jacobi evaluations proportional to its least prime factor. Every check that appears to gate the guard passes identically with it removed, these square rows included
PrimeField64.IsBaillieProbablePrime over the swept candidate stream, forced odd
Legs.Against: Oracles.ExactPrimality — the exact decision, outside Puck.Maths entirely. ENVELOPE, the same one the two IsPrime laws state and stated again because this stream lives almost entirely above it: through 8191² = 67092481 that oracle decides by TRIAL DIVISION alone and shares no idea with the subject, but above that band it runs twenty BigInteger strong-probable-prime rounds whose base set OPENS WITH TWO — the very round that is one of the two halves of IsBaillieProbablePrime. So above the trial-division band subject and oracle share that CRITERION, differing in arithmetic (one shared ScaledResidueRing64 against plain residues), in base set and in loop structure; the swept stream draws full-width raws, so essentially every candidate lands there. What this leg pins independently is the Lucas half and the composition, not the base-two round in isolation — prime-field.strong-round-vs-oracle owns that. Below 2^64 the composition is not merely unrefuted but VERIFIED counterexample-free: Feitsma and Galway independently enumerated the complete set of base-two Fermat pseudoprimes below 2^64 (the strong ones being a derived subset) and no member is simultaneously a strong Lucas pseudoprime for Selfridge Method A, which is exactly what this implementation runs. ulong IS that region, so nothing here is extrapolated and the equality is asserted flatly. The failure message says outright that a disagreement below 2^64 is either a defect or the first known counterexample — which is the honest reading, not a hedge

Legs.Subject: the CARRIAGE, read back rather than assumed: IsBaillieProbablePrime is exactly IsStrongProbablePrime(value, 2) AND IsStrongLucasProbablePrime(value), both halves evaluated separately and the conjunction compared. That is one line of source, and a line that could carry a disjunction or transposed operands — neither of which the differential against a primality oracle would show. It is asserted on a FIXED ladder as well as on the swept stream, and the ladder is where it actually bites: on any sampled stream the two halves AGREE at every candidate — every prime passes both, every composite fails both, which is exactly the Baillie-PSW guarantee — so the conjunction is decidable only at the published pseudoprime populations, where the round accepts alone at 2047 and the Lucas half accepts alone at 5459. The claim body COUNTS both directions and fails if the ladder ever stops carrying one

ENVELOPE, measured rather than assumed, and it corrects what a reader would expect: the WITNESS BASE in that line is NOT pinned by this law or by anything else in the suite. Swapping the base two for the base three moves no answer at any odd value below 10^7, and a value below 2^64 that moved one would have to be a composite passing both the base-three round and the strong Lucas test — a Baillie-PSW counterexample in its own right, of exactly the class Feitsma and Galway's enumeration rules out for base two. A DEGENERATE base is a different matter and IS caught: bases 0, 1 and value itself all collapse the round to a constant true, and the ladder's Lucas-pseudoprime rows reject that at 5459

ENVELOPE: this law SAMPLES where prime-field.baillie-psw-exhaustive is exhaustive at EVERY one of the 4,294,967,296 values a uint holds — against a segmented sieve of Eratosthenes, not against another Puck.Maths decision — and where it replays 160,000 sampled and 60,000 contiguous values to ulong.MaxValue against Oracles.ExactPrimality. That law is the gate of record for SCALE, at the Exhaustive tier; the statements are here, at Default. Neither replaces the other
the two pseudoprime POPULATIONS below 10^4, ENUMERATED by the subjects themselves rather than looked up — every odd composite in the band is offered to the base-two round and to the strong Lucas test
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeSieve, an ordinary sieve of Eratosthenes, which decides which candidates are composite in the first place and so fixes the band the enumeration runs over. It carries no notion of a witness, a base or a Lucas parameter, so it shares with the subjects not merely no code but no idea. Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out

Legs.Subject: the composition's whole THESIS, checked instead of asserted: the two enumerated populations are DISJOINT. That is the only reason a conjunction of two probable-prime tests is worth more than either half

the sole-rejecter controls, which make both halves demonstrably load-bearing rather than decorative: the base-two round ACCEPTS every strong Lucas pseudoprime, so the Lucas half is what rejects it; the Lucas test ACCEPTS every base-two strong pseudoprime, so the round is what rejects it; and the composition rejects both populations. This is probable-ness pinned as a FACT — these tests are REQUIRED to accept composites, and the law says so rather than apologising for it
IsPrime rejects every value in both populations and every Carmichael number, which is what separates the exact decision from the two probable ones on exactly the values where they differ
the smallest values, where the guards outnumber the arithmetic: 0, 1 and the small composites are rejected by both tests and by the composition; every prime below 100 is accepted by all three

This law is the gate of record for SCALE: prime-field.is-prime-vs-witness-oracle and prime-field.pow-vs-modpow remain the gates of record for the statements at Default, and this law is where the exhaustive 0..10^6 sweep and the contiguous 100,000-value band at 9·10^11 actually run. Both halves of the composition are PROBABLE-prime tests with infinitely many pseudoprimes each, so the composition earns its trust from evidence; this leg is that evidence, and it makes the statement below 2^32 a COMPUTED fact rather than a cited one — no known counterexample becomes none exists. The reference shares with the subject not merely no code but no idea, and is not a second Puck.Maths kernel. The work is embarrassingly parallel and the VERDICT is not — each block records only its own least disagreement and the blocks are read in ascending order — so a rerun reports the same value. Measured: about 49 seconds

The failure message says outright that a disagreement below 2^64 is either a defect or the first known counterexample. The reference is outside the library entirely rather than a second decision in the same class, such as PrimeExtensions.IsPrime

Legs.Subject: the composition's THESIS, checked instead of asserted: the two enumerated populations are DISJOINT. On any sampled stream the two halves agree at every candidate, which is exactly the Baillie-PSW guarantee, so the conjunction is decidable ONLY at these populations

the degenerate shapes: 2,999 small perfect squares and eight squares of large primes are rejected, where no small factor screens the value out and the Selfridge search would otherwise run to its least prime factor; the d = 1 and s = 1 ladders at every width from 2^2 to 2^64, where one end puts the whole test in the squaring loop and the other never enters it; and every Fibonacci and Lucas term the carrier holds with its two neighbours on each side — the world the D = 5 parameter generates, which is the Lucas test's own worst case
